claim: CGEL excludes passive be inside the complement of active perception see. It allows get or a bare past participial.
evidence_summary: CNN and CBS transcripts attest eventive be-passives with agentive by-phrases. An ABC concordance reports a return to see the car be unearthed. Sheehan accepts I saw him be fired.
finding: Active see licenses embedded verbal be-passives for some speakers and contexts. The evidence leaves relative frequency and the historical distribution in literal perception open.
proposed_wording: Active perception see can take a bare past participial or an embedded passive with get or be. The availability of be can vary by speaker and context.
inference: Must an embedded passive after active perception see lack the auxiliary be?

evidence.passage: Ch. 14 §5.4, p. 1237 [43] and n. 42, and Ch. 16 §10.1.4, p. 1442 [53ii]. CGEL accepts get or a bare participial and stars passive be within the complement of active perception see.
evidence.example: You saw the President be contradicted by intelligence chiefs. The next sentence uses you saw the president lash out.
evidence.establishes: The same speaker uses the same perception verb and embedded subject with a verbal passive and an active predicate in consecutive sentences.
evidence.locator: Segment 03, Jim Sciutto’s question about Tuesday’s testimony.

evidence.source: CBS Face the Nation (17 May 2015), Peggy Noonan.
evidence.passage: Ch. 14 §5.4, p. 1237 [43] and n. 42, and Ch. 16 §10.1.4, p. 1442 [53ii]. CGEL accepts get or a bare participial and stars passive be within the complement of active perception see.
evidence.example: It’s been interesting to see the President be cuffed about and rebuffed publicly, followed by an agentive by-phrase.
evidence.establishes: The coordinated verbal participles refer to observed public events in the preceding weeks.
evidence.locator: Roundtable, Peggy Noonan’s turn after Bob Schieffer’s comment about the king.

evidence.source: ABC Good Morning America (2007), supplied COCA concordance. Link to the memoir for the event context.
evidence.passage: Ch. 14 §5.4, p. 1237 [43] and n. 42, and Ch. 16 §10.1.4, p. 1442 [53ii]. CGEL accepts get or a bare participial and stars passive be within the complement of active perception see.
evidence.example: Returned a half century later to see the car be unearthed.
evidence.establishes: The purpose clause describes intended witnessing of a physical event. Forrest’s memoir corroborates the excavation context. The wording is from the supplied concordance.

evidence.source: Michelle Sheehan (2018). On why verbs of perception/causation sometimes don’t passivize. Olomouc Linguistics Colloquium abstract.
evidence.passage: Ch. 14 §5.4, p. 1237 [43] and n. 42, and Ch. 16 §10.1.4, p. 1442 [53ii]. CGEL accepts get or a bare participial and stars passive be within the complement of active perception see.
evidence.example: Sheehan’s example set [3a] presents I saw him be fired and I heard him be fired as grammatical.
evidence.establishes: A published counterjudgment to the ban. The broadcaster examples independently attest active see with the embedded passive.
